A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2M study. All 23 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–H, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original dialogue and summarization experiments, reward-model accuracy, computational costs and ablations in Section 5, plus hidden-state analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and the appendices, including benchmark scores, ablations and hidden-state similarity measurements.

M1.justification: The policy-feedback inputs, sequence-to-token cross-attention, time-dependent weighting, GREBT objective and iterative update procedure are unchanged in Section 4 and Algorithm 1.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval 2, MT-Bench and TL;DR coverage, including the same hidden-state test scenarios. Newly cited benchmarks and vision research are not added to the experiments.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1, 2 and 4: SFT, ReMax, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO and the corresponding reward-model variants remain in the same comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same models, sampling procedures, preprocessing, sample sizes, training budgets and evaluation metrics. No existing setting is revised or new evaluation protocol introduced.

E4.justification: The noise, frozen-training and BT/GRE ablations, training-dynamics and computational analyses, and appendix case study and hidden-state analyses are retained. Their questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: The correlation statistics and statistical presentation of the tables and plots are unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed counts, repeated-run information, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 1–9 retain the same results. For example, RLOO+R2M's TL;DR win rate remains 81.6%, and Table 5's similarities remain 0.67, 0.75 and 0.45; relocating Table 5 does not change its findings.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1 and 4.1, their definitions, assumptions, proofs and corollaries in Appendix A, and the mathematical material in Appendices G and H are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about using policy hidden states for lightweight real-time reward-model alignment, mitigating overoptimization and improving performance with marginal overhead.

C2.justification: Interpretations of policy feedback, group degeneration, training dynamics and computational efficiency remain unchanged, as do applicability and broader-impact statements. The added related-work text introduces no substantive qualification or mechanism explanation for R2M.

D1.justification: The algorithm, hyperparameters, model identifiers, data-processing instructions and training details in Section 5 and Appendices E, G and H are retained. Appendix H.2 adds citations without adding implementation details or changing resource-access information.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds references to recent algorithm variants and a short discussion of representation learning, image restoration, tracking and normalization. Appendix H.2 adds further citations, while R2M's central positioning against reward-overoptimization methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 corrects the running-header text, changes the affiliation from ByteDance Seed to Bytedance China, and expands Appendix B with a short contextual passage. The remaining prose and section hierarchy are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The template running header is replaced by the paper title, and references and later appendices reflow. Figure 9 shifts within page 19 and Table 5 moves from page 19 to page 20, without changes to their content or design.

improvement.justification: Correcting the template header provides modest editorial polish. The additions in Appendices B and H.2 mainly broaden citations without materially clarifying R2M's positioning or strengthening its argument. With the scientific evidence, proofs and reproducibility information unchanged, overall quality is essentially stable.
